creator: Alexander Terp
description: Muster's banner (MIP-9) takes Esc itself while its reply field holds marked text: it discards the composition and keeps the keyboard in the reply, so a composition no input method ends (a dead key's accent, or marked text with no input method taking Esc) is never stranded. The cost: SwiftUI's onKeyPress sees Esc before the text view hands it to the input context, so an input method that handles Esc in steps (Kotoeri reverts a conversion before dropping it) never gets the key, and one Esc drops the whole composition. MIP-9 section 7 says to leave an input method's composition alone. A better shape gives the input context first refusal (NSTextInputContext.handleEvent on the current event) and discards only a composition it left unchanged, but that needs a real input method to test, which the contract tier does not drive today. Stage 2's message box will meet the same question.
title: Esc in a banner's reply discards an input method's composition at once, rather than letting the input method step back
